title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第32部分：虚拟内存

chapters.Frontier: 15. 前沿：翻译覆盖范围与分层内存
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

9a5cd79b9659.en: Two copies of the same program run on our machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each stores its process number at the same address, hexadecimal four oh five, oh oh four. Then each steps aside, so the other can store its number at that very address. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then each reads the address back. Process one finds one, and process two finds two. <bookmark mark='c'/> They used the same address, and two different bytes of memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every address a program uses is virtual. The hardware translates it, on every load, store and instruction fetch, through a table the kernel keeps for that process. This part builds that translation into Pebble, and asks what it costs and what it buys.
9a5cd79b9659.zh: 同一个程序的两个副本在我们的机器上运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个副本都把自己的进程号存到同一个地址：十六进制的四零五零零四。然后各自让出处理器，好让另一个把自己的号码存到这个地址上。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着每个都把这个地址读回来。进程一读到一，进程二读到二。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们用的是同一个地址，却是两个不同的内存字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>程序使用的每一个地址都是虚拟的。硬件在每一次读、写和取指令时，都通过内核为这个进程维护的一张表来翻译它。这一部分把这种翻译做进 Pebble，并追问它的代价是什么、又换来了什么。

df2a1b8c5565.en: Part 32 of Computer Science, Built: Virtual Memory. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: why programs need relocation and protection, and why pages won; page tables, the tree the hardware walks on every access, and the cache that makes it fast, measured on this machine; page faults, and what a trip to the disk costs; which page to throw out when memory is full, with the optimum, a famous anomaly, and the policies in real systems; copy-on-write, the kernel's own mapping and Meltdown, and the kernel's allocators; and virtual machines and containers, with our own operating system running on a hypervisor we write.
df2a1b8c5565.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第32部分：虚拟内存。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：程序为什么需要重定位和保护，以及页为什么胜出；页表，硬件在每次访问时遍历的那棵树，以及让它变快的缓存，在这台机器上实测；缺页，以及一趟磁盘之旅的代价；内存满了时该扔掉哪一页，包括最优解、一个著名的异常和真实系统中的策略；写时复制、内核自己的映射与 Meltdown，以及内核的分配器；还有虚拟机和容器，我们自己的操作系统将运行在我们亲手写的虚拟机监控器上。

458a70560c50.en: In Part 31, PebbleOS gave each process its own region of physical memory. <bookmark mark='a'/> The tokenizer was compiled to run at one mebibyte and the job at two, and each program worked only there. That caused four problems. <bookmark mark='b'/> Relocation: a program runs only where it was linked, so a second copy needs a second compile, and fork, which copies a process, is impossible. <bookmark mark='c'/> Protection: the bounds guard one contiguous range, so two processes cannot share a library, and code cannot be read-only. <bookmark mark='d'/> Size: a program can never be bigger than its region. <bookmark mark='e'/> And fragmentation, which the next chapter shows. <bookmark mark='f'/> The fix for all four is the same: give each process its own virtual addresses, and have the hardware translate every one.
458a70560c50.zh: 在第31部分，PebbleOS 给每个进程一块自己的物理内存区域。<bookmark mark='a'/>分词器被编译成在一兆字节处运行，那项任务在两兆字节处，每个程序只能在那里工作。这带来了四个问题。<bookmark mark='b'/>重定位：程序只能在链接时指定的位置运行，所以第二个副本需要再编译一次，而复制一个进程的 fork 根本做不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>保护：界限寄存器只守护一段连续的范围，所以两个进程不能共享一个库，代码也不能设为只读。<bookmark mark='d'/>大小：程序永远不能大于它的区域。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有碎片，下一章会展示。<bookmark mark='f'/>四个问题的解决办法是同一个：给每个进程它自己的虚拟地址，让硬件翻译每一个地址。

3f95c9deb486.en: The idea came from Manchester. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Atlas computer had a small fast core memory, and a drum six times larger and far slower. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its designers let programs address one large memory, and had the machine move fixed-size pages of five hundred and twelve words between core and drum, automatically, as they were needed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each page of core had a register holding the number of the page it currently held. An address whose page matched one of them ran at full speed; otherwise the machine trapped and fetched the page. <bookmark mark='d'/> Tom Kilburn and his colleagues called it a one-level storage system, in 1962. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every phone, laptop and server since works the same way, with RAM and flash in place of core and drum.
3f95c9deb486.zh: 这个想法来自曼彻斯特。<bookmark mark='a'/>Atlas 计算机有一块小而快的磁芯存储器，和一个大六倍、慢得多的磁鼓。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的设计者让程序寻址一块大的存储器，由机器自动地、按需地在磁芯和磁鼓之间搬运五百一十二个字的固定大小的页。<bookmark mark='c'/>磁芯的每一页都有一个寄存器，记着它当前装的是哪一页。地址所在的页若与其中之一相符，就全速运行；否则机器陷入，把那一页取来。<bookmark mark='d'/>汤姆·基尔伯恩和同事们在1962年称之为单级存储系统。<bookmark mark='e'/>此后每一部手机、笔记本和服务器都以同样的方式工作，只是用内存和闪存代替了磁芯和磁鼓。

358a30ea776d.en: Chapter two. Base and bounds, and segments.
358a30ea776d.zh: 第2章。基址与界限，以及段。

fa7993738cce.en: The simplest translation adds a base. <bookmark mark='a'/> The process uses addresses from zero. The hardware first checks each one against a bound, and faults if it is too big. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then it adds the base, the physical address where the kernel put this process. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two registers, one addition and one comparison, and the process can be loaded anywhere, and cannot touch anything outside its range. Part 31 had the bounds; adding the base gives relocation too. <bookmark mark='d'/> Segments generalise it: a separate base and bound for the code, the data, the heap and the stack, so each can grow on its own, and code can be shared. <bookmark mark='e'/> The Burroughs B5000 had segments in 1961, and Intel's 8086 in 1978. Modern x86 processors have all but abandoned them, for a reason the next picture shows.
fa7993738cce.zh: 最简单的翻译是加上一个基址。<bookmark mark='a'/>进程使用从零开始的地址。硬件先把每个地址和界限比较，太大就报错。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后加上基址，也就是内核放置这个进程的物理地址。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个寄存器，一次加法和一次比较，进程就能装在任何地方，而且碰不到它范围之外的任何东西。第31部分已有界限；加上基址，就有了重定位。<bookmark mark='d'/>段把它推广：代码、数据、堆和栈各有一对基址和界限，于是每一段都能独自增长，代码也能共享。<bookmark mark='e'/>Burroughs B5000 在1961年就有了段，英特尔 8086 在1978年也有。现代 x86 处理器几乎完全放弃了它们，原因就在下一张图里。

561c7c0125ab.en: The trouble with segments is that they come in every size. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated a thousand and twenty-four units of memory, with segments of random sizes arriving and leaving, each placed in the first hole big enough. Here is the memory at the end: live segments in colour, holes outlined in red. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first refusal came early: a request for ninety units, when a hundred and thirty-eight were free, but split among eight holes, the largest sixty-three. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over the whole run, two hundred and forty-seven requests were refused. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is the problem of malloc from Part 11, now inside the kernel. <bookmark mark='e'/> Memory can be compacted by moving segments together, but every process must stop while it is copied. <bookmark mark='f'/> The way out is to make every piece the same size. Then any free piece fits any request. That piece is a page.
561c7c0125ab.zh: 段的麻烦在于它们大小各异。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了一千零二十四个单位的内存，大小随机的段不断到来和离开，每段放进第一个足够大的空洞。这是运行结束时的内存：彩色的是活着的段，红框是空洞。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一次拒绝来得很早：一个九十单位的请求，而空闲的有一百三十八个，却分散在八个空洞里，最大的只有六十三。<bookmark mark='c'/>整个运行中，有两百四十七个请求被拒绝。<bookmark mark='d'/>这正是第11部分 malloc 的问题，如今出现在内核里。<bookmark mark='e'/>可以把段挪到一起来紧缩内存，但复制时每个进程都得停下来。<bookmark mark='f'/>出路是让每一块都一样大。这样任何空闲块都能满足任何请求。这样的一块就叫页。

9153e5863a25.en: Paging cuts memory into pieces of one size, four kibibytes in our machine, and translates each piece separately. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the address from the start of this part, in binary. <bookmark mark='b'/> The low twelve bits are the offset within the page, and pass through untouched. <bookmark mark='c'/> The high twenty bits are the virtual page number, and that is what gets translated. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our hardware splits the page number again, into two ten-bit indexes, for the two levels of table you will see in a moment. <bookmark mark='e'/> And because every frame of physical memory is the same size, any free frame can hold any page. Fragmentation between pieces is gone; at most part of the last page of each region is wasted.
9153e5863a25.zh: 分页把内存切成同样大小的块，在我们的机器上是四 KiB，并分别翻译每一块。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是本部分开头的那个地址，写成二进制。<bookmark mark='b'/>低十二位是页内偏移，原样通过。<bookmark mark='c'/>高二十位是虚拟页号，要翻译的正是它。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的硬件把页号再分成两个十位的索引，对应你马上会看到的两级表。<bookmark mark='e'/>而且因为物理内存的每个页框大小相同，任何空闲页框都能装任何页。块与块之间的碎片消失了；最多浪费每个区域最后一页的一部分。

a374b8d92ea0.en: Each entry in a page table is one word. <bookmark mark='a'/> The top twenty bits name the physical frame. The low bits are flags. <bookmark mark='b'/> Valid means the page is mapped at all. Read, write and execute say what may be done with it, so code can be execute-only and data never executed. User says whether a user-mode program may touch it. <bookmark mark='c'/> And two bits are set by the hardware itself: accessed, on every use, and dirty, on every write. <bookmark mark='d'/> The kernel reads them back. Accessed tells it which pages are in use, which chapter seven needs; dirty tells it which pages must be written to disk before their frame is reused.
a374b8d92ea0.zh: 页表的每一项是一个字。<bookmark mark='a'/>高二十位指明物理页框。低位是标志。<bookmark mark='b'/>有效位表示这一页是否映射了。读、写、执行三位说明可以对它做什么，于是代码可以只执行，数据永远不被执行。用户位说明用户态程序能不能碰它。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有两位由硬件自己设置：访问位，每次使用时设置；脏位，每次写入时设置。<bookmark mark='d'/>内核把它们读回来。访问位告诉它哪些页在用，第7章需要它；脏位告诉它哪些页在页框被重用前必须写回磁盘。

821ac077a607.en: Now the walk itself, done in hardware on every access that misses the cache of chapter five. <bookmark mark='a'/> The control register p-t-b-r holds the physical address of the current process's first-level table. The first ten bits of the address pick an entry there, which points to a second-level table. <bookmark mark='b'/> The next ten bits pick an entry in that, which names the frame. Add the offset, and that is the physical address. <bookmark mark='c'/> The two processes use the same indexes, but their tables, built by the kernel, point to different frames, so the same address holds one in one process and two in the other. <bookmark mark='d'/> Entry zero of every first-level table is the same: it maps the kernel, as chapter ten explains.
821ac077a607.zh: 现在看遍历本身，每当访问在第5章的那个缓存中未命中时，由硬件完成。<bookmark mark='a'/>控制寄存器 ptbr 保存当前进程一级表的物理地址。地址的前十位在那里选出一项，它指向一张二级表。<bookmark mark='b'/>接下来的十位在二级表中选出一项，它指明页框。加上偏移，就是物理地址。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个进程用的索引相同，但它们由内核建立的表指向不同的页框，所以同一个地址在一个进程里装着一，在另一个里装着二。<bookmark mark='d'/>每张一级表的第零项都相同：它映射内核，第10章会解释。

246d3010a16c.en: Why two levels? A flat table, one entry for each of the million pages in a thirty-two-bit address space, would need four mebibytes per process, almost all of it saying not mapped. <bookmark mark='a'/> Instead the table is a tree. The first level has a thousand and twenty-four entries, each covering four mebibytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> In our processes only two are used: entry zero maps the kernel with one large page, and entry one points to the process's second-level table. <bookmark mark='c'/> That table has entries for the pages actually mapped. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each level resolves ten bits of the page number, like the tries of Part 21. <bookmark mark='e'/> An empty first-level entry covers four mebibytes with no second-level table at all. <bookmark mark='f'/> So our process needs eight kibibytes of table instead of four mebibytes. <bookmark mark='g'/> The price is a memory read per level on every translation.
246d3010a16c.zh: 为什么要两级？一张平坦的表，三十二位地址空间里的一百万页每页一项，每个进程需要四 MiB，几乎全都写着“未映射”。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以表是一棵树。第一级有一千零二十四项，每项覆盖四 MiB。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的进程中只用了两项：第零项用一个大页映射内核，第一项指向进程的二级表。<bookmark mark='c'/>那张表只为真正映射的页设项。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一级解析页号的十位，就像第21部分的字典树。<bookmark mark='e'/>一个空的一级表项覆盖四 MiB，根本不需要二级表。<bookmark mark='f'/>所以我们的进程只需要八 KiB 的页表，而不是四 MiB。<bookmark mark='g'/>代价是每次翻译每一级都要读一次内存。

d519623f3133.en: Real machines go deeper. <bookmark mark='a'/> For our thirty-two-bit addresses, a flat table would be four mebibytes. For x86-64's forty-eight bits, five hundred and twelve gibibytes, per process. <bookmark mark='b'/> So x86-64 uses four levels of nine bits each, with five hundred and twelve eight-byte entries in each four-kibibyte table. <bookmark mark='c'/> Since 2019, servers can use five levels, for fifty-seven-bit addresses, so a miss in the translation cache can cost five memory reads before the real one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Some designs invert the table instead, with one entry per physical frame, found by hashing the virtual page number; PowerPC and Itanium did this.
d519623f3133.zh: 真实的机器层级更深。<bookmark mark='a'/>对我们的三十二位地址，平坦的表是四 MiB。对 x86-64 的四十八位，每个进程五百一十二 GiB。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以x86-64 用四级，每级九位，每张四 KiB 的表有五百一十二个八字节的表项。<bookmark mark='c'/>从2019年起，服务器可以用五级，支持五十七位地址，于是翻译缓存的一次未命中，在真正的读之前可能要读五次内存。<bookmark mark='d'/>有些设计把表倒过来，每个物理页框一项，用虚拟页号的哈希来查找；PowerPC 和 Itanium 就是这样做的。

52cd48c79e23.en: Chapter five. The translation lookaside buffer.
52cd48c79e23.zh: 第5章。快表，即翻译后备缓冲器。

9103c186e756.en: A walk costs two extra memory reads in our machine, and up to five on a modern one, for every single access. The fix is a small cache of recent translations, the translation lookaside buffer, which IBM's 360 model 67 had in 1967. <bookmark mark='a'/> We ran the Job as two processes under paged PebbleOS, with TLBs of different sizes. <bookmark mark='b'/> With four entries, three and a half percent of accesses miss and need a walk. With eight, under one percent. With sixteen, one access in eleven thousand: the working set of both programs fits. <bookmark mark='c'/> But every context switch writes a new page-table root, and our hardware then flushes the TLB. Switching every five hundred instructions, the misses rise eightfold. Tag each entry with the address space it belongs to, an address-space identifier, and the entries survive the switch: forty-three misses instead of five hundred and eight. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real processors have two levels of TLB, with tags, which x86 calls process-context identifiers.
9103c186e756.zh: 在我们的机器上，一次遍历要多读两次内存，在现代机器上最多五次，而且是每一次访问都要。解决办法是一个保存最近翻译的小缓存，即翻译后备缓冲器，简称 TLB，IBM 360 的 67 型在1967年就有了。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们在分页的 PebbleOS 上把那项任务作为两个进程来运行，用不同大小的 TLB。<bookmark mark='b'/>四项时，百分之三点五的访问未命中，需要遍历。八项时，不到百分之一。十六项时，一万一千次访问才有一次：两个程序的工作集都装得下。<bookmark mark='c'/>但每次上下文切换都会写入新的页表根，我们的硬件随之清空 TLB。每五百条指令切换一次，未命中增加到八倍。给每一项标上它所属的地址空间，即地址空间标识符，表项就能熬过切换：四十三次未命中，而不是五百零八次。<bookmark mark='d'/>真实的处理器有两级 TLB，带有标识，x86 称之为进程上下文标识符。

27b58d3ba271.en: On this machine we can watch the TLB from outside. <bookmark mark='a'/> A program follows a chain of pointers through more and more pages, touching one cache line in each, and we time each step. <bookmark mark='b'/> Up to sixty-four pages, each step takes under two nanoseconds: every translation is in the first-level TLB. <bookmark mark='c'/> Past sixty-four, the time jumps: the second-level TLB is slower. <bookmark mark='d'/> Far past it, the steps climb as walks begin, and the caches themselves fill. At sixty-five thousand pages, a step takes about a hundred nanoseconds. <bookmark mark='e'/> Now repeat with two-mebibyte pages. The program touches exactly the same cache lines, but each TLB entry now covers five hundred and twelve times more memory, and the step falls to under sixty nanoseconds. <bookmark mark='f'/> That is why databases and virtual machines ask for huge pages, and why Linux builds them automatically where it can.
27b58d3ba271.zh: 在这台机器上，我们可以从外面观察 TLB。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个程序沿着一串指针穿过越来越多的页，每页只碰一个缓存行，我们为每一步计时。<bookmark mark='b'/>不超过六十四页时，每步不到两纳秒：每个翻译都在一级 TLB 里。<bookmark mark='c'/>超过六十四页，时间跳了一级：二级 TLB 更慢。<bookmark mark='d'/>再往后，遍历开始了，缓存本身也满了，每步的时间不断攀升。到六万五千页时，一步约一百纳秒。<bookmark mark='e'/>现在换成两 MiB 的页再来一遍。程序碰的缓存行完全相同，但每个 TLB 项覆盖的内存多了五百一十二倍，每步降到不到六十纳秒。<bookmark mark='f'/>这就是数据库和虚拟机要求大页的原因，也是 Linux 在可能时自动建立大页的原因。

cf1d291925d4.en: What happens when a program touches a page that is not mapped? <bookmark mark='a'/> It executes a store. The TLB has no entry, so the hardware walks the table, and finds the entry not valid. <bookmark mark='b'/> It traps, with cause fifteen and the address in t-val. <bookmark mark='c'/> The kernel checks that the address lies inside the process's memory, and takes a free frame. It fills the frame: with zeros for a new page of heap or stack, or with data read from the disk. It writes the entry, and returns with e-ret to the very same store, which now succeeds. <bookmark mark='d'/> The faulting instruction never happened, so it can simply happen again. <bookmark mark='e'/> This is demand paging: map nothing until it is touched. <bookmark mark='f'/> PebbleOS now does it. A program that touches sixteen new pages of heap takes sixteen faults, each about three thousand three hundred kernel instructions, nearly all of them writing the zeros.
cf1d291925d4.zh: 程序碰到一个没有映射的页时会发生什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>它执行一条存储指令。TLB 里没有这一项，于是硬件遍历页表，发现表项无效。<bookmark mark='b'/>它陷入，原因是十五，地址放在 tval 里。<bookmark mark='c'/>内核检查这个地址是否在进程的内存范围之内，然后取一个空闲页框。它填充这个页框：新的堆页或栈页填零，否则从磁盘读入数据。它写好表项，用 eret 返回到同一条存储指令，这一次就成功了。<bookmark mark='d'/>出错的指令从未真正执行过，所以它可以简单地再执行一次。<bookmark mark='e'/>这就是按需调页：在被碰到之前什么都不映射。<bookmark mark='f'/>PebbleOS 现在就这样做。一个碰了十六个新堆页的程序发生十六次缺页，每次大约三千三百条内核指令，几乎全都在写零。

a12ab15c290c.en: When memory is full, a fault must first free a frame, and the page in it has to go somewhere. <bookmark mark='a'/> The dirty bit from chapter three decides where. <bookmark mark='b'/> A clean page, unchanged since it was read from a file, can simply be dropped: if it is needed again, it is read again. <bookmark mark='c'/> A dirty page must be written out first, and a page of heap or stack has no file at all, so it goes to swap space, a partition or file set aside for exactly this. <bookmark mark='d'/> That doubles the cost of the fault. On the Job's trace, with eight frames under LRU, forty-four percent of evictions are dirty. <bookmark mark='e'/> So kernels do not wait for the fault. A page-out daemon, kswapd in Linux, writes dirty pages back in the background, in batches, and keeps a pool of free frames ready, so that a fault only has to read.
a12ab15c290c.zh: 内存满了时，一次缺页必须先腾出一个页框，而其中的页总得有个去处。<bookmark mark='a'/>第3章的脏位决定它去哪里。<bookmark mark='b'/>干净的页，自从从文件读入后没有改过，可以直接丢掉：如果再需要，就再读一次。<bookmark mark='c'/>脏页必须先写出去，而堆页或栈页根本没有文件，所以只能去交换空间，那是专门为此留出的一个分区或文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>这让缺页的代价翻倍。在那项任务的序列上，用 LRU、八个页框时，百分之四十四的换出是脏页。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以内核不等缺页发生。一个换出守护进程，Linux 里叫 kswapd，在后台成批地把脏页写回，并备好一池空闲页框，让缺页时只需要读。

1a2657dfe48e.en: How much does a fault cost? <bookmark mark='a'/> On this machine, touching a page that is already mapped takes twenty-five nanoseconds. The first touch of a brand-new page, a fault plus zeroing four kibibytes, takes almost two microseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> A fault that must read from storage is far worse: around a hundred microseconds from flash, and eight milliseconds from a spinning disk. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the average cost of a memory access depends on how often it faults. <bookmark mark='d'/> With a disk, one fault in a thousand accesses makes memory eighty times slower. Even one in a million adds eight percent. <bookmark mark='e'/> A system that pages to disk is usable only while faults are rarer than one in a million, which is why running out of memory feels like falling off a cliff.
1a2657dfe48e.zh: 一次缺页要花多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>在这台机器上，碰一个已经映射的页要二十五纳秒。第一次碰一个全新的页，一次缺页加上把四 KiB 清零，要将近两微秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>必须从存储设备读取的缺页要糟得多：从闪存约一百微秒，从机械硬盘八毫秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以一次内存访问的平均代价取决于它多常缺页。<bookmark mark='d'/>用磁盘时，一千次访问里有一次缺页，内存就慢八十倍。即使一百万次里一次，也要多出百分之八。<bookmark mark='e'/>一个换页到磁盘的系统，只有在缺页比百万分之一还少时才可用，这就是内存耗尽时感觉像跌下悬崖的原因。

213afa659483.en: Chapter seven. Which page to evict.

d6b4ee1ecd92.en: When memory is full and a fault needs a frame, some page must go. <bookmark mark='a'/> Which one? <bookmark mark='b'/> László Belady showed in 1966 that the best choice is the page whose next use lies farthest in the future. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here it is on the reference string Belady used, with three frames: seven faults, and no policy can do better. <bookmark mark='d'/> The proof is an exchange, like the one for shortest-first scheduling in Part 31. Suppose some schedule, at a fault, evicts a page f, where the optimum would evict e, so f is needed again before e. <bookmark mark='e'/> Change it to evict e, and then copy the old schedule. When f is next requested, the new schedule either hits, or pays the single fault the old one would have paid anyway. So the new schedule is never worse, and agrees with the optimum one step longer. <bookmark mark='f'/> But this optimum needs to know the future. It is a yardstick, not a policy. Real policies guess the future from the past.
d6b4ee1ecd92.zh: 内存满了，而一次缺页需要一个页框时，必须有某一页离开。<bookmark mark='a'/>哪一页？<bookmark mark='b'/>拉斯洛·贝拉迪在1966年证明，最好的选择是下一次使用在最遥远未来的那一页。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是它在贝拉迪所用的引用串上、三个页框时的表现：七次缺页，没有任何策略能做得更好。<bookmark mark='d'/>证明是一个交换论证，就像第31部分里最短作业优先的那个。假设某个调度在一次缺页时换出页 f，而最优解会换出 e，于是 f 会在 e 之前再被需要。<bookmark mark='e'/>把它改为换出 e，然后照搬原来的调度。当 f 下一次被请求时，新调度要么命中，要么付出原调度本来也要付出的那一次缺页。所以新调度绝不会更差，而且与最优解多一致了一步。<bookmark mark='f'/>但这个最优解需要知道未来。它是一把尺子，而不是一个策略。真实的策略只能根据过去猜测未来。

e0423f883a1a.en: The simplest guess is first in, first out: evict the page that was loaded longest ago. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the reference string Belady used, with three frames. Each column is one reference; the red dots are faults. Nine faults. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now give FIFO a fourth frame. Ten faults. More memory, more faults. <bookmark mark='c'/> Belady, Nelson and Shedler published this in 1969, and it shocked people, because it means buying memory can make a machine slower. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is rare: we found two such strings in twenty thousand random ones. But it can happen, and some policies cannot do it at all.
e0423f883a1a.zh: 最简单的猜法是先进先出：换出装入最久的那一页。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是贝拉迪用的引用串，三个页框。每一列是一次引用；红点是缺页。九次缺页。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在给 FIFO 第四个页框。十次缺页。内存更多，缺页更多。<bookmark mark='c'/>贝拉迪、尼尔森和谢德勒在1969年发表了这个结果，它让人们大吃一惊，因为这意味着买更多内存可能让机器变慢。<bookmark mark='d'/>它很罕见：两万个随机串里我们只找到两个。但它确实会发生，而有些策略根本不可能出现它。

f0629d43f661.en: A better guess: the past predicts the future. Evict the page used least recently. <bookmark mark='a'/> On Belady's string, least recently used is worse than FIFO at three frames, but never shows the anomaly. <bookmark mark='b'/> The reason is the inclusion property. <bookmark mark='c'/> With k frames, LRU holds exactly the k pages used most recently; with k plus one, the k plus one most recent, which include them. <bookmark mark='d'/> So any reference that hits with k frames also hits with more, and adding memory can never add faults. Algorithms with this property are called stack algorithms, and OPT is one too. <bookmark mark='e'/> We checked five thousand random strings: no anomalies for LRU.
f0629d43f661.zh: 更好的猜法：过去预示未来。换出最久没有使用的那一页。<bookmark mark='a'/>在贝拉迪的串上，最近最少使用在三个页框时比 FIFO 还差，但从不出现异常。<bookmark mark='b'/>原因是包含性质。<bookmark mark='c'/>k 个页框时，LRU 恰好持有最近使用的 k 个页；k 加一个时，持有最近的 k 加一个，其中包括前者。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以任何在 k 个页框时命中的引用，在更多页框时也命中，增加内存永远不会增加缺页。有这种性质的算法叫栈算法，OPT 也是其中之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们检查了五千个随机串：LRU 没有任何异常。

07a235038372.en: How far from the optimum can LRU be? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take four pages used in a cycle, with three frames. LRU always evicts exactly the page that comes next, so it faults on every single reference. <bookmark mark='b'/> The optimum, knowing the future, faults only once in every three. Over a hundred and twenty references: a hundred and twenty faults against forty-two. With k frames, an adversary can make any deterministic policy fault about k times as often as the optimum. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sleator and Tarjan proved in 1985 that this is the worst: LRU, and FIFO too, are within a factor k of the optimum, and no deterministic policy can promise better. More usefully, give LRU k frames and the optimum only h: the factor falls to k over k minus h plus one, under two when LRU has twice the memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> On the Job's real trace it is better still. With twice the memory, LRU does not merely come within a factor of two. It beats the optimum outright. Real programs are not adversaries.
07a235038372.zh: LRU 离最优解能有多远？<bookmark mark='a'/>取四个页循环使用，三个页框。LRU 总是恰好换出下一个要用的页，所以每一次引用都缺页。<bookmark mark='b'/>知道未来的最优解，大约每三次才缺一次。在一百二十次引用上：一百二十次缺页，对四十二次。有 k 个页框时，对手能让任何确定性策略的缺页约为最优解的 k 倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>斯利特和塔扬在1985年证明这就是最坏情况：LRU，还有 FIFO，都在最优解的 k 倍之内，而没有任何确定性策略能保证更好。更有用的是，给 LRU k 个页框、最优解只给 h 个：倍数降到 k 除以 k 减 h 加一，当 LRU 有两倍内存时不到二。<bookmark mark='d'/>在那项任务的真实序列上还要更好。有两倍内存时，LRU 不只是在两倍之内，而是直接胜过最优解。真实的程序不是对手。

d3d8ff150e87.en: True LRU would reorder a list on every memory access, far too often for hardware or software. The practical approximation is CLOCK. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each frame keeps the accessed bit the hardware sets. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a fault, a hand sweeps around the frames. A frame whose bit is set gets a second chance: the bit is cleared and the hand moves on. The first frame found with its bit clear is evicted. <bookmark mark='c'/> Nothing happens on ordinary accesses, only on faults. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real kernels refine the idea, and newer policies, 2Q, ARC and LIRS, also defend against a single scan flushing everything useful, as the next chapter shows.
d3d8ff150e87.zh: 真正的 LRU 要在每次内存访问时重排一个列表，无论对硬件还是软件都太频繁了。实用的近似是时钟算法。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个页框保存硬件设置的访问位。<bookmark mark='b'/>缺页时，一根指针绕着页框扫过。访问位已置的页框得到第二次机会：清掉这一位，指针继续前进。第一个访问位为零的页框被换出。<bookmark mark='c'/>普通访问时什么也不做，只在缺页时动作。<bookmark mark='d'/>真实的内核改进了这个想法，而更新的策略，2Q、ARC 和 LIRS，还能防止一次扫描冲掉所有有用的页，下一章会展示。

bdde7cfaa424.en: Chapter eight. Working sets, and thrashing.

85c34abeb692.en: How do the policies compare on a real program? <bookmark mark='a'/> We recorded every memory reference of the Job on a sixteen-kilobyte passage, a hundred and twenty thousand of them, to thirty-nine pages of one kibibyte, and replayed them through each policy at every memory size. <bookmark mark='b'/> With eight frames, the optimum takes twelve thousand faults, LRU twenty-three thousand, and FIFO twenty-nine thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> LRU sits between the optimum and FIFO, with CLOCK close behind it. <bookmark mark='d'/> And because LRU is a stack algorithm, its whole curve comes from a single pass over the trace, by recording how deep each page is in the recency stack when it is used again: Mattson and his colleagues' trick from 1970, which caches are still sized with. <bookmark mark='e'/> With forty frames everything fits, and only the first touches fault.
85c34abeb692.zh: 这些策略在真实程序上比较起来如何？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们记录了那项任务在一段十六千字节的文本上的每一次内存引用，共十二万次，涉及三十九个一 KiB 的页，并在每一种内存大小下把它们重放给每一种策略。<bookmark mark='b'/>八个页框时，最优解缺页一万两千次，LRU 两万三千次，FIFO 两万九千次。<bookmark mark='c'/>LRU 处在最优解和 FIFO 之间，时钟算法紧随其后。<bookmark mark='d'/>而且因为 LRU 是栈算法，它的整条曲线只需扫一遍序列就能得到：记录每一页再次被使用时在最近使用栈中有多深。这是马特森和同事们在1970年的技巧，至今仍用来确定缓存的大小。<bookmark mark='e'/>四十个页框时一切都装得下，只有第一次接触才缺页。

2e620ab6e56e.en: Here is that trick worked by hand, on eight references. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep the pages in a stack, most recently used on top. For each reference, find how deep its page is: that depth is its stack distance. A page never seen before has distance infinity. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then move it to the top. Page b is found at depth two, a at depth three, c at depth four. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the key fact. LRU with k frames holds exactly the top k pages of this stack, so a reference hits precisely when its distance is at most k. <bookmark mark='d'/> Count the distances greater than k, and you have LRU's misses: eight with one frame, seven with two, five with three, four with four. <bookmark mark='e'/> One pass gives every memory size at once. That is how the whole LRU curve came from a single pass over the Job's trace, and how cache sizes are still chosen.
2e620ab6e56e.zh: 下面在八次引用上手算这个技巧。<bookmark mark='a'/>把页放在一个栈里，最近使用的在顶上。对每次引用，找出它的页有多深：这个深度就是它的栈距离。从未见过的页，距离为无穷大。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后把它移到顶上。页 b 在深度二被找到，a 在深度三，c 在深度四。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在是关键的事实。k 个页框的 LRU 恰好持有这个栈最上面的 k 页，所以一次引用命中，当且仅当它的距离不超过 k。<bookmark mark='d'/>数一数大于 k 的距离，就得到 LRU 的缺页数：一个页框八次，两个七次，三个五次，四个四次。<bookmark mark='e'/>扫一遍就得到所有内存大小的结果。整条 LRU 曲线就是这样从那项任务序列的一遍扫描中得到的，至今缓存的大小也还是这样选的。

823dbb38637d.en: LRU has a famous weakness. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a trace like a database's: twenty hot pages used over and over, and then a scan through sixty pages, used once, again and again. <bookmark mark='b'/> With thirty-two frames, LRU faults on almost every reference, and so does CLOCK. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each scan pushes the hot pages out just before they are needed again, because the scanned pages are more recent. <bookmark mark='d'/> The adaptive replacement cache, ARC, keeps two lists, pages seen once and pages seen twice, and moves the boundary between them as it learns. LIRS ranks pages by the distance between their last two uses, so a page used once never displaces a page used often. Both do far better, and LIRS approaches the optimum.
823dbb38637d.zh: LRU 有一个著名的弱点。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一条像数据库那样的序列：二十个热页反复使用，然后是对六十个页的一次扫描，每页只用一次，如此循环往复。<bookmark mark='b'/>三十二个页框时，LRU 几乎每次引用都缺页，时钟算法也一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>每次扫描都在热页再次被需要之前把它们挤出去，因为被扫描的页更新。<bookmark mark='d'/>自适应替换缓存 ARC 维护两个列表，只见过一次的页和见过两次的页，并在学习中移动两者的分界。LIRS 按一页最近两次使用之间的距离给页排序，所以只用一次的页永远不会挤掉常用的页。两者都好得多，LIRS 接近最优。

b2e433755ac0.en: Peter Denning gave the idea that ties this together. <bookmark mark='a'/> A program's working set at time t is the set of pages it used in the last tau references. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here it is along the Job's trace, for three windows: in any hundred references the Job uses about nine pages, over longer ones it reaches all thirty-nine. <bookmark mark='c'/> Denning's rule for a time-shared machine: keep each running process's working set in memory, and if they do not all fit, run fewer processes.
b2e433755ac0.zh: 彼得·丹宁给出了把这一切串起来的思想。<bookmark mark='a'/>程序在时刻 t 的工作集，是它在最近 τ 次引用中用过的页的集合。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是沿着那项任务的序列、三种窗口下的工作集：任意一百次引用中，那项任务大约用九个页；在更长的窗口里，它会用到全部三十九个。<bookmark mark='c'/>丹宁为分时机器定下的规则：把每个运行中进程的工作集都留在内存里；如果装不下，就少运行几个进程。

4ac2b3e2bad0.en: Break that rule and you get thrashing. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated processes sharing sixty-four frames, each with a working set of twenty pages, and each sometimes waiting for ordinary input or output. <bookmark mark='b'/> With more processes, the processor fills the waits with other work, up to half busy with three. <bookmark mark='c'/> But four working sets of twenty do not fit in sixty-four frames. Now every process faults, each fault waits for the one disk, and utilisation falls. <bookmark mark='d'/> At eight processes the processor is almost idle, and the disk never stops: the machine is all paging. <bookmark mark='e'/> Operating systems in the sixties learned to respond by taking whole processes out of memory; Linux, when memory is truly exhausted, kills one.
4ac2b3e2bad0.zh: 违反这条规则，就会抖动。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了若干进程共享六十四个页框，每个进程的工作集为二十页，并且时不时要等待普通的输入输出。<bookmark mark='b'/>进程越多，处理器就用其他工作填满等待，三个进程时忙到一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>但四个二十页的工作集装不进六十四个页框。这时每个进程都缺页，每次缺页都要等那一个磁盘，利用率下降。<bookmark mark='d'/>八个进程时处理器几乎闲着，磁盘却从不停歇：机器全在换页。<bookmark mark='e'/>六十年代的操作系统学会了把整个进程移出内存来应对；Linux 在内存真正耗尽时，会杀掉一个进程。

08c1567924ed.en: Chapter nine. Copy-on-write, zero pages, and memory-mapped files.
08c1567924ed.zh: 第9章。写时复制、零页与内存映射文件。

5ed7ab764c6e.en: Fork promises the child a copy of all the parent's memory. Virtual memory lets it keep that promise without copying. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fork copies only the page tables, so both processes point at the same frames, and it marks every page read-only in both. <bookmark mark='b'/> Reading costs nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> When either process writes a page, the write faults. The kernel sees a page that is shared, not truly read-only, copies it into a fresh frame, maps the copy writable for the writer, and lets the write go ahead. <bookmark mark='d'/> Only pages that are actually written are ever copied. A fork followed at once by exec, the shell's pattern, copies almost nothing. The Mach kernel made this standard in the late nineteen-eighties.
5ed7ab764c6e.zh: fork 承诺给子进程一份父进程全部内存的副本。虚拟内存让它不用复制就能兑现承诺。<bookmark mark='a'/>fork 只复制页表，于是两个进程指向同样的页框，并把两边的每一页都标为只读。<bookmark mark='b'/>读不花任何代价。<bookmark mark='c'/>当任一进程写一页时，这次写会出错。内核看到这一页是共享的，并非真的只读，就把它复制到一个新页框，把副本以可写方式映射给写的一方，再让这次写继续。<bookmark mark='d'/>只有真正被写的页才会被复制。fork 之后立刻 exec，也就是外壳的做法，几乎什么都不复制。Mach 内核在八十年代后期让这成为标准做法。

4051c7589f43.en: On this machine: <bookmark mark='a'/> a parent using two hundred and fifty-six mebibytes forks in under six milliseconds, because only the tables are copied. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the child writes one byte in every page. Each first write takes three microseconds: a fault, and a copy of four kibibytes. <bookmark mark='c'/> A second write to the same page takes twenty-six nanoseconds, an ordinary store. <bookmark mark='d'/> Part 31's fork with a gibibyte took thirty-three milliseconds, all of it tables. <bookmark mark='e'/> And a child that writes all its memory still pays for the copy in the end, one fault at a time.
4051c7589f43.zh: 在这台机器上：<bookmark mark='a'/>一个使用两百五十六 MiB 的父进程 fork 不到六毫秒，因为只复制了页表。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后子进程在每一页写一个字节。每页的第一次写要三微秒：一次缺页，加上复制四 KiB。<bookmark mark='c'/>对同一页的第二次写要二十六纳秒，一次普通的存储。<bookmark mark='d'/>第31部分里带一 GiB 的 fork 用了三十三毫秒，全花在页表上。<bookmark mark='e'/>而一个写遍自己全部内存的子进程，最终还是要为复制买单，一次缺页一次缺页地付。

61f1c09b4b32.en: The same machinery, mapping and faulting, serves three more purposes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Memory a process has asked for but never written reads as zeros from one shared frame of zeros, and the first write gives it a private page. <bookmark mark='b'/> m-map puts a file's pages into the address space, so reading the file is just a load; the pages come from the kernel's cache of the disk. <bookmark mark='c'/> Shared libraries, the libc of Part 11, are mapped read-only into every process from the same frames, so a hundred processes hold one copy. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price is that a load from a mapped file can, invisibly, wait for the disk.
61f1c09b4b32.zh: 同样的机制，映射加缺页，还有三个用途。<bookmark mark='a'/>进程申请了却从未写过的内存，从一个共享的全零页框读出零，第一次写时才得到私有的一页。<bookmark mark='b'/>mmap 把文件的页放进地址空间，于是读文件只是一次读内存；这些页来自内核对磁盘的缓存。<bookmark mark='c'/>共享库，第11部分的 libc，从同样的页框以只读方式映射进每个进程，所以一百个进程只持有一份副本。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是，从映射文件的一次读，可能不知不觉地要等磁盘。

048a77614db3.en: Chapter ten. The kernel's own mapping.

1458cdc9c577.en: Where does the kernel itself live? <bookmark mark='a'/> In every process's address space. The same kernel pages appear in every page table, marked supervisor-only: user mode cannot touch them, but they are always there. <bookmark mark='b'/> So a trap needs no change of page table: the kernel's code and data are already mapped. <bookmark mark='c'/> In our PebbleOS it is entry zero of every first-level table, a single four-mebibyte page. A user program that reads it faults and is killed. <bookmark mark='d'/> And because the process's pages are mapped too, the kernel can copy a process's buffers using the very addresses the process passed it.
1458cdc9c577.zh: 内核自己住在哪里？<bookmark mark='a'/>在每个进程的地址空间里。同样的内核页出现在每一张页表中，标为仅限内核态：用户态碰不到它们，但它们一直在那里。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以陷入时不需要切换页表：内核的代码和数据已经映射好了。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们的 PebbleOS 中，它是每张一级表的第零项，一个四 MiB 的页。读它的用户程序会出错并被杀掉。<bookmark mark='d'/>而且因为进程的页也映射着，内核可以直接用进程传给它的地址来复制进程的缓冲区。

5b710423b9f7.en: In 2018 that arrangement broke. <bookmark mark='a'/> Meltdown, which Part 8 previewed: on many Intel processors, a user-mode load from a kernel address did fault, but only after the out-of-order core had already used the data speculatively. <bookmark mark='b'/> The data leaked through the cache, so the supervisor bit alone no longer kept the kernel secret. <bookmark mark='c'/> The fix was kernel page-table isolation. Each process gets two tables: in user mode almost none of the kernel is mapped, just the few pages that handle the entry. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every system call and interrupt must now switch tables. With address-space tags the switch is cheap; without them, it flushes the TLB each time, and some workloads slowed by a third. <bookmark mark='e'/> This machine's processor reports itself not affected, because newer chips fixed the flaw in hardware, and Linux skips the isolation here.
5b710423b9f7.zh: 2018年，这种安排被打破了。<bookmark mark='a'/>Meltdown，第8部分预告过：在许多英特尔处理器上，用户态从内核地址读取确实会出错，但乱序核心在那之前已经推测性地用过这份数据了。<bookmark mark='b'/>数据通过缓存泄露出来，于是仅靠内核态标志位已经不能保住内核的秘密。<bookmark mark='c'/>解决办法是内核页表隔离。每个进程有两张表：在用户态几乎不映射内核，只映射处理入口的几页。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在每次系统调用和中断都必须切换页表。有地址空间标识时，切换很便宜；没有时，每次都要清空 TLB，有些负载慢了三分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>这台机器的处理器报告自己不受影响，因为更新的芯片在硬件里修复了这个缺陷，Linux 在这里就跳过了隔离。

7ac7be83706c.en: Chapter eleven. How the kernel allocates memory for itself.
7ac7be83706c.zh: 第11章。内核如何为自己分配内存。

592500da6593.en: The kernel needs memory too: for page tables, process control blocks, network buffers. It takes it in physical frames, and the classic allocator for frames is the buddy system, from Knowlton in 1965. <bookmark mark='a'/> Memory is kept in blocks whose sizes are powers of two. A request for three pages rounds up to four. <bookmark mark='b'/> There is no free block of four, so the sixteen splits into two eights, and one eight into two fours. The first four is handed out; its halves' partners stay on the free lists. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each block's partner, its buddy, is found by flipping one bit of its address. <bookmark mark='d'/> So freeing is quick: if the buddy is free too, merge, and try again one size up. Fragmentation can never leave two free buddies side by side.
592500da6593.zh: 内核也需要内存：用于页表、进程控制块、网络缓冲区。它以物理页框为单位取用，而页框的经典分配器是伙伴系统，出自1965年的诺尔顿。<bookmark mark='a'/>内存保存在大小为二的幂的块中。三页的请求向上取整为四页。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有空闲的四页块，于是十六页分裂成两个八页，其中一个八页再分裂成两个四页。第一个四页交出去；被分出的另一半留在空闲链表上。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个块的伙伴，通过翻转它地址中的一位就能找到。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以释放很快：如果伙伴也空闲，就合并，再到大一级重试。碎片永远不会让两个空闲的伙伴并排躺着。

e6152caf3f7e.en: Run it under random traffic: a thousand and twenty-four pages, three thousand steps, each one allocating between one and thirty pages or freeing an earlier block. <bookmark mark='a'/> Blocks split five hundred and eighty-three times and merged five hundred and seventeen times. <bookmark mark='b'/> Not one request was refused: there was always a free block of at least a quarter of the pool, usually half. <bookmark mark='c'/> Chapter two's segments, in the same size of pool, refused two hundred and forty-seven. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price is waste inside the blocks: five pages occupy a block of eight. <bookmark mark='e'/> Linux uses exactly this for physical frames, with eleven sizes, from one page to a thousand and twenty-four, and you can read the free lists in proc buddy-info.
e6152caf3f7e.zh: 让它承受随机的流量：一千零二十四页，三千步，每一步要么分配一到三十页，要么释放之前的一个块。<bookmark mark='a'/>块分裂了五百八十三次，合并了五百一十七次。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有一个请求被拒绝：始终有一个至少四分之一池大小的空闲块，通常是一半。<bookmark mark='c'/>第2章的段，在同样大小的池里，拒绝了两百四十七个。<bookmark mark='d'/>代价是块内部的浪费：五页要占一个八页的块。<bookmark mark='e'/>Linux 正是用它来管理物理页框，有十一种大小，从一页到一千零二十四页，你可以在 /proc/buddyinfo 里读到空闲链表。

546ca43cd192.en: And here are this machine's own free lists, read just now from proc buddy-info. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each bar is one order: single pages on the left, four-mebibyte blocks on the right. <bookmark mark='b'/> There are almost six gibibytes free. <bookmark mark='c'/> Nearly half of it is in the largest blocks, ready to be split for any request, or to become huge pages. <bookmark mark='d'/> And there are only eight free single pages: freed pages almost always find their buddy and merge. <bookmark mark='e'/> On a busy machine that has run for weeks, the high orders run dry. Then a request for a huge page has to wait for compaction: the kernel moves pages around, updating their mappings, to rebuild large free blocks.
546ca43cd192.zh: 这是这台机器自己的空闲链表，刚刚从 /proc/buddyinfo 读出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>每根柱子是一个阶：左边是单页，右边是四 MiB 的块。<bookmark mark='b'/>空闲的将近六 GiB。<bookmark mark='c'/>其中将近一半在最大的块里，随时可以为任何请求分裂，或者变成大页。<bookmark mark='d'/>而空闲的单页只有八个：释放的页几乎总能找到伙伴并合并。<bookmark mark='e'/>在一台跑了好几个星期的繁忙机器上，高阶的块会用光。这时一次大页请求就得等待紧缩：内核把页挪来挪去，同时更新它们的映射，以重建大的空闲块。

31c705462d41.en: But most of what a kernel allocates is small: a socket, an open file, a process control block of a hundred bytes or so. A page each would be absurd. <bookmark mark='a'/> Jeff Bonwick's slab allocator, written for SunOS in 1994, keeps a cache for each kind of object. Each cache carves pages into slots of exactly that size: fifty-six objects of seventy-two bytes in one page. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ten thousand such objects take forty-one megabytes at a page each, and under three quarters of a megabyte in slabs. <bookmark mark='c'/> And Bonwick's second idea: a freed object goes back to its slab still initialised, so the next allocation of that type can skip setting it up. <bookmark mark='d'/> Linux's allocator, called SLUB, descends from it; slab-top shows its caches on any Linux machine.
31c705462d41.zh: 但内核分配的大部分东西都很小：一个套接字、一个打开的文件、一个一百字节左右的进程控制块。每个给一页就太荒唐了。<bookmark mark='a'/>杰夫·邦威克1994年为 SunOS 写的 slab 分配器，为每一种对象保留一个缓存。每个缓存把页切成恰好那么大的槽：一页装五十六个七十二字节的对象。<bookmark mark='b'/>一万个这样的对象，每个一页要四十一兆字节，用 slab 不到四分之三兆字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有邦威克的第二个想法：释放的对象回到它的 slab 时仍保持初始化状态，于是同类对象的下一次分配可以省去初始化。<bookmark mark='d'/>Linux 的分配器叫 SLUB，就源于它；在任何 Linux 机器上，slabtop 都能显示它的缓存。

13d36de28019.en: Virtual memory gives each process a private memory. The same trick, applied to the whole machine, gives each operating system a private computer. IBM's VM three-seventy did it in 1972. <bookmark mark='a'/> Run the guest kernel, unmodified, in user mode, under a small hypervisor that alone has the real privilege. <bookmark mark='b'/> Whenever the guest kernel does something privileged, such as writing a control register, it traps. The hypervisor performs the operation on a copy of the registers it keeps for that guest, and returns. <bookmark mark='c'/> Popek and Goldberg made the condition precise in 1974. Call an instruction sensitive if it reads or changes the machine's mode, its control state or its devices. <bookmark mark='d'/> Call it privileged if it traps in user mode. <bookmark mark='e'/> If every sensitive instruction is privileged, trap-and-emulate works. <bookmark mark='f'/> Pebble passes: all four privileged instructions, and every touch of the device page, trap in user mode. <bookmark mark='g'/> And when a guest's own process makes a system call, the hypervisor reflects it: it saves the program counter and sets the cause in the guest's virtual registers, as the hardware would, and jumps to the guest kernel.
13d36de28019.zh: 虚拟内存给每个进程一块私有的内存。同样的技巧用在整台机器上，就给每个操作系统一台私有的计算机。IBM 的 VM/370 在1972年就做到了。<bookmark mark='a'/>把客户机内核原封不动地放在用户态运行，下面是一个小小的虚拟机监控器，只有它拥有真正的特权。<bookmark mark='b'/>每当客户机内核做特权操作，比如写控制寄存器，它就会陷入。监控器在它为这个客户机保存的寄存器副本上完成这个操作，然后返回。<bookmark mark='c'/>波佩克和戈德堡在1974年把条件说得精确。如果一条指令读取或改变机器的模式、控制状态或设备，就称它为敏感指令。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果它在用户态会陷入，就称它为特权指令。<bookmark mark='e'/>如果每条敏感指令都是特权指令，陷入并模拟就行得通。<bookmark mark='f'/>Pebble 通过了：全部四条特权指令，以及对设备页的每一次访问，在用户态都会陷入。<bookmark mark='g'/>当客户机自己的进程发起系统调用时，监控器把它转交回去：像硬件那样，在客户机的虚拟寄存器里保存程序计数器、设置原因，然后跳到客户机内核。

af02dfd63d1f.en: We built that hypervisor for Pebble, and ran Part 31's kernel under it without changing one instruction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two processes printing letters: the guest kernel exited to the hypervisor almost six hundred times, mostly to read and write control registers during its context switches. <bookmark mark='b'/> The output is identical to the native run, and so is the number of instructions the guest executed: the guest cannot tell. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Job's pipeline tells a different story. It moves four thousand six hundred bytes through the console device, and almost every exit is a device access, one per byte. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is why real hypervisors offer paravirtual devices, as Xen did in 2003 and virtio does today: the guest knows it is virtual and hands over a whole buffer with a single exit.
af02dfd63d1f.zh: 我们为 Pebble 写了这样一个监控器，并在它上面运行第31部分的内核，一条指令都没改。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个打印字母的进程：客户机内核退出到监控器将近六百次，大多是在上下文切换中读写控制寄存器。<bookmark mark='b'/>输出与原生运行完全相同，客户机执行的指令数也一样：客户机察觉不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>那项任务的流水线讲的是另一个故事。它通过控制台设备传送四千六百字节，几乎每一次退出都是一次设备访问，每字节一次。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是真实的监控器提供半虚拟化设备的原因，Xen 在2003年就这样做，今天的 virtio 也是：客户机知道自己是虚拟的，一次退出交出整个缓冲区。

29c977161413.en: The x86, the processor in most computers, failed Popek and Goldberg's test. <bookmark mark='a'/> Robin and Irvine later counted seventeen sensitive instructions that do not trap. One, pop-flags, run in user mode, silently ignores the bit that turns interrupts off, so a guest kernel cannot even tell that it failed. <bookmark mark='b'/> VMware's answer, in 1999, was binary translation: rewrite the guest kernel's code as it runs, replacing the troublesome instructions, while letting user code run directly. <bookmark mark='c'/> Xen's answer, in 2003, was to modify the guest kernel to call the hypervisor openly. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then Intel and AMD added a new mode beneath the kernel, and x86 passed the test. <bookmark mark='e'/> Surprisingly, Adams and Agesen measured the first hardware version as slower than VMware's software, because every exit was so expensive.
29c977161413.zh: x86，大多数计算机里的处理器，没有通过波佩克和戈德堡的检验。<bookmark mark='a'/>罗宾和欧文后来数出十七条不会陷入的敏感指令。其中一条 popf，在用户态运行时会悄悄忽略关中断的那一位，所以客户机内核甚至不知道自己失败了。<bookmark mark='b'/>VMware 在1999年的答案是二进制翻译：在客户机内核的代码运行时改写它，替换掉麻烦的指令，而用户代码直接运行。<bookmark mark='c'/>Xen 在2003年的答案是修改客户机内核，让它公开地调用监控器。<bookmark mark='d'/>后来英特尔和 AMD 在内核之下增加了一种新模式，x86 通过了检验。<bookmark mark='e'/>出人意料的是，亚当斯和阿格森测得第一代硬件方案比 VMware 的软件还慢，因为每次退出都太昂贵了。

6102f601ca2f.en: Memory needs virtualising too. The guest kernel builds page tables from what it thinks are physical addresses; the hypervisor has its own table from those to the real ones. <bookmark mark='a'/> Modern hardware walks both. Each guest table entry lives at a guest-physical address, so before the hardware can read it, it must walk the host's four levels to find it, and only then read it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Four guest levels times five references, plus four more to translate the final address: twenty-four memory references for one TLB miss, where a native walk takes four. <bookmark mark='c'/> In general, n plus one times m plus one, minus one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Before this hardware existed, hypervisors kept shadow page tables, combining the two, and had to catch every change the guest made to its own tables. <bookmark mark='e'/> Nested paging, from AMD in 2007 and Intel in 2008, ended that, at the price of the two-dimensional walk, which is why huge pages matter even more inside virtual machines.
6102f601ca2f.zh: 内存也需要虚拟化。客户机内核用它以为是物理地址的东西建立页表；监控器有自己的一张表，把这些地址映射到真正的地址。<bookmark mark='a'/>现代硬件两张表都遍历。每个客户机表项位于一个客户机物理地址上，所以硬件在读它之前，必须先遍历主机的四级找到它，然后才能读。<bookmark mark='b'/>四个客户机层级，每级五次引用，再加四次翻译最终地址：一次 TLB 未命中要二十四次内存引用，而原生遍历只要四次。<bookmark mark='c'/>一般地，是 n 加一乘以 m 加一，再减一。<bookmark mark='d'/>在这种硬件出现之前，监控器维护影子页表，把两张表合二为一，还得捕捉客户机对自己页表的每一次修改。<bookmark mark='e'/>嵌套分页，AMD 在2007年、英特尔在2008年推出，结束了这种做法，代价是二维的遍历，这也是大页在虚拟机里更加重要的原因。

a7696401b5e1.en: A virtual machine is one way to give a program its own world. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each guest brings its own kernel, running on a hypervisor. <bookmark mark='b'/> A container is the other way. There is one kernel, and it simply shows different groups of processes different views: their own process numbers, their own files, their own network and users. <bookmark mark='c'/> A container starts in milliseconds and carries no second kernel. But all the containers on a machine trust the same kernel, and that is the price we will come back to.
a7696401b5e1.zh: 虚拟机是给程序一个自己的世界的一种办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个客户机带着自己的内核，运行在监控器上。<bookmark mark='b'/>容器是另一种办法。只有一个内核，它只是向不同的进程组展示不同的视图：它们自己的进程号、自己的文件、自己的网络和用户。<bookmark mark='c'/>容器几毫秒就能启动，不带第二个内核。但一台机器上的所有容器都信任同一个内核，这就是我们稍后要回头讨论的代价。

927613226f30.en: On Linux the views are called namespaces. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is one made on this machine, without any special privilege: a new user namespace and a new process namespace, and a shell inside them. <bookmark mark='b'/> The shell believes it is process number one, and that it is root, user zero. Ask it for the list of processes and it sees three: itself and the two commands it just ran. Outside, this machine is running eighty-two. <bookmark mark='c'/> There are eight kinds of namespace: processes, the file tree, the network, user ids, and four smaller ones. <bookmark mark='d'/> The second ingredient is control groups, which limit how much of each resource a group of processes may use: processor time, memory, the number of processes, and so on. <bookmark mark='e'/> Add a file tree to run in, and you have a container. Docker, in 2013, put the three together in a form everyone could use.
927613226f30.zh: 在 Linux 上，这些视图叫命名空间。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是在这台机器上创建的一个，不需要任何特殊权限：一个新的用户命名空间和一个新的进程命名空间，里面跑着一个外壳。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个外壳以为自己是一号进程，而且是 root，用户零。让它列出进程，它只看到三个：它自己和它刚运行的两个命令。在外面，这台机器正运行着八十二个。<bookmark mark='c'/>命名空间有八种：进程、文件树、网络、用户编号，以及四种小一些的。<bookmark mark='d'/>第二种成分是控制组，它限制一组进程能用多少各种资源：处理器时间、内存、进程数等等。<bookmark mark='e'/>再加上一棵用来运行的文件树，就是一个容器。Docker 在2013年把这三者组合成人人都能用的形式。

ed03e45dd9dd.en: Side by side. <bookmark mark='a'/> A virtual machine boots a kernel, in seconds; a container starts a process, in milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each virtual machine holds a whole guest kernel in memory; containers share one kernel and its cache of the disk. <bookmark mark='c'/> But a virtual machine's only door to the host is the hypervisor and its few kinds of exit. A container's door is the whole Linux system call interface, some four hundred and fifty calls. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a single kernel bug can break out of every container. <bookmark mark='e'/> In 2016, Dirty COW, a race in exactly the copy-on-write code of chapter nine, let any process write to files it could only read. <bookmark mark='f'/> The industry's answer is a middle ground: Google's gVisor puts a second kernel in user space, and Amazon's Firecracker builds virtual machines small enough to boot in about a hundred and twenty-five milliseconds. <bookmark mark='g'/> Amazon's serverless functions each run in one.
ed03e45dd9dd.zh: 并排比较。<bookmark mark='a'/>虚拟机要启动一个内核，几秒钟；容器只是启动一个进程，几毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个虚拟机在内存里装着一整个客户机内核；容器共享一个内核及其磁盘缓存。<bookmark mark='c'/>但虚拟机通往主机的唯一的门是监控器和它那几种退出。容器的门是整个 Linux 系统调用接口，大约四百五十个调用。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以一个内核漏洞就能突破所有容器。<bookmark mark='e'/>2016年的 Dirty COW，正是第9章写时复制代码里的一个竞争，让任何进程都能写它只能读的文件。<bookmark mark='f'/>业界的答案是折中：谷歌的 gVisor 在用户空间放第二个内核，亚马逊的 Firecracker 把虚拟机做得足够小，大约一百二十五毫秒就能启动。<bookmark mark='g'/>亚马逊的无服务器函数，每一个都运行在这样的虚拟机里。

691ba7b169b6.en: Chapter fourteen. PebbleOS gains virtual memory.
691ba7b169b6.zh: 第14章。PebbleOS 有了虚拟内存。

5c299acdcf2d.en: Our own machine has had all of this since chapter three. Here is what it took. <bookmark mark='a'/> The hardware: a memory-management unit for Pebble, with the two-level walk, a sixteen-entry TLB, and three new kinds of fault. <bookmark mark='b'/> The boot loader builds one page table per process, with the kernel's superpage in entry zero, the code pages readable and executable, and the data pages readable and writable. <bookmark mark='c'/> The context switch gains two instructions, to load and write the page-table base register, which also flushes the TLB. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the trap handler gains this: a page fault at an address inside the process's range, on a page not yet mapped, gets a fresh frame, zeroed, mapped, and the instruction runs again. <bookmark mark='e'/> Any other fault kills the process, as it did in Part 31. <bookmark mark='f'/> In all, forty-six instructions: the kernel grew from two hundred and eighty-four to three hundred and thirty.
5c299acdcf2d.zh: 从第3章起，我们自己的机器就已经有了这一切。下面是它所需要的。<bookmark mark='a'/>硬件：Pebble 的内存管理单元，带两级遍历、十六项的 TLB，以及三种新的错误。<bookmark mark='b'/>引导程序为每个进程建一张页表，第零项是内核的超级页，代码页可读可执行，数据页可读可写。<bookmark mark='c'/>上下文切换多了两条指令，读入并写入页表基址寄存器，这也会清空 TLB。<bookmark mark='d'/>陷阱处理程序多了这一段：在进程范围之内、尚未映射的页上的缺页，得到一个清零的新页框，映射好，指令再执行一次。<bookmark mark='e'/>其他任何错误都杀掉进程，就像第31部分那样。<bookmark mark='f'/>总共四十六条指令：内核从两百八十四条增长到三百三十条。

cc17146e7478.en: Here is the whole page table of the hook's first process, read out of our machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> The library's code, then three pages of buffers for input and output, then the program's own code, and its data page, holding the cell from the hook. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then two hundred and forty-nine pages that were never mapped, and at the very top, the stack. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bits tell the story. Code is readable and executable, never writable; data is writable, never executable; every page is marked for user mode; and the hardware has set accessed and dirty as the program ran. The output buffer is dirty because the program printed. <bookmark mark='d'/> Seven pages of the two hundred and fifty-six are mapped: twenty-eight kibibytes of memory for a one-mebibyte address space. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the stack sits a whole mebibyte above the code, with nothing in between to pay for: room for both to grow.
cc17146e7478.zh: 这是开头那个第一个进程的整张页表，从我们的机器里读出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>库的代码，然后是三页输入输出缓冲区，然后是程序自己的代码，以及它的数据页，里面装着开头的那个单元。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是两百四十九个从未映射的页，而在最顶端，是栈。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些位说明了一切。代码可读可执行，从不可写；数据可写，从不可执行；每一页都标为用户态可用；硬件在程序运行时设置了访问位和脏位。输出缓冲区是脏的，因为程序打印了东西。<bookmark mark='d'/>两百五十六页中映射了七页：一兆字节的地址空间只用了二十八 KiB 内存。<bookmark mark='e'/>而栈位于代码之上整整一 MiB 处，中间什么都不用付钱：两者都有增长的余地。

9f1ba7d4da15.en: Now four processes on one machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> One prints eight letters A. <bookmark mark='b'/> One stores a zero over its own first instruction. Its code page is mapped, but not writable: a store fault, cause fifteen, and the kernel kills it. <bookmark mark='c'/> One loads from an address beyond its memory: a load fault, cause thirteen, killed. <bookmark mark='d'/> And one walks up its heap, touching sixteen new pages. It takes sixteen page faults, each served with a zeroed frame, and prints a G. <bookmark mark='e'/> The console shows only the survivors' output. <bookmark mark='f'/> A write to code is a protection fault; a wild load is outside the process altogether. <bookmark mark='g'/> In both cases the hardware only reports, the kernel decides, and the other processes never notice.
9f1ba7d4da15.zh: 现在，一台机器上四个进程。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个打印八个字母 A。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个把零写到自己的第一条指令上。它的代码页映射了，但不可写：一次存储错误，原因十五，内核杀掉它。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个从它内存之外的地址读取：一次读取错误，原因十三，被杀掉。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有一个沿着它的堆往上走，碰了十六个新页。它发生十六次缺页，每次得到一个清零的页框，然后打印一个 G。<bookmark mark='e'/>控制台上只有幸存者的输出。<bookmark mark='f'/>写代码是保护错误；野读则完全在进程之外。<bookmark mark='g'/>两种情况下，硬件只负责报告，由内核决定，其他进程毫无察觉。

057120166faa.en: Finally, the pipeline that has run through this series: the tokenizer feeding the Job, as two processes, now each in its own address space. <bookmark mark='a'/> Without paging, Part 31's kernel ran it in five hundred and fifty-eight thousand instructions. <bookmark mark='b'/> Paged, with every page mapped at boot, it takes just twelve more. <bookmark mark='c'/> Paged with zero pages on demand, it takes seven page faults and twenty-two thousand more instructions. <bookmark mark='d'/> The output is identical, byte for byte. <bookmark mark='e'/> So translation itself is almost free: two instructions for the table register at each switch, and the TLB hides the rest. <bookmark mark='f'/> A demand fault costs about three thousand instructions, nearly all of them zeroing. <bookmark mark='g'/> What demand paging buys is memory: the two processes need twenty-four frames instead of a hundred and forty-six, because most of the Job's hash table is never touched.
057120166faa.zh: 最后，是贯穿这套课程的那条流水线：分词器向那项任务供数据，作为两个进程，现在各自在自己的地址空间里。<bookmark mark='a'/>不分页时，第31部分的内核用五十五万八千条指令运行它。<bookmark mark='b'/>分页，并在启动时映射所有页，只多了十二条。<bookmark mark='c'/>分页并按需提供零页，发生七次缺页，多了两万两千条指令。<bookmark mark='d'/>输出逐字节相同。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以翻译本身几乎是免费的：每次切换为页表寄存器多两条指令，其余都由 TLB 藏起来了。<bookmark mark='f'/>一次按需缺页大约三千条指令，几乎全在清零。<bookmark mark='g'/>按需调页换来的是内存：两个进程只需要二十四个页框，而不是一百四十六个，因为那项任务的哈希表大部分从未被碰过。

8bd70c161f7c.en: Chapter fifteen. The frontier: translation reach, and memory in tiers.
8bd70c161f7c.zh: 第15章。前沿：翻译覆盖范围与分层内存。

5ff2168092da.en: The first frontier is reach: how much memory the TLB can translate without walking. <bookmark mark='a'/> A first-level data TLB of sixty-four entries, with four-kibibyte pages, covers two hundred and fifty-six kibibytes, less than this machine's second-level cache. The second-level TLB, with fifteen hundred entries, covers six mebibytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> A laptop has sixteen gibibytes; a large server, four tebibytes, a million times the reach. <bookmark mark='c'/> Huge pages multiply the reach by five hundred and twelve, or by a quarter of a million. <bookmark mark='d'/> On chapter five's staircase, a pointer chase over two hundred and fifty-six mebibytes took forty percent less time with two-mebibyte pages. <bookmark mark='e'/> But a huge page wastes memory when only a little of it is used, and it needs two mebibytes of contiguous physical frames, which a busy machine's buddy allocator may not have.
5ff2168092da.zh: 第一个前沿是覆盖范围：TLB 不用遍历就能翻译多少内存。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个六十四项的一级数据 TLB，用四 KiB 的页，覆盖两百五十六 KiB，比这台机器的二级缓存还小。二级 TLB 有一千五百项，覆盖六 MiB。<bookmark mark='b'/>一台笔记本有十六 GiB；一台大服务器有四 TiB，是覆盖范围的一百万倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>大页把覆盖范围放大五百一十二倍，或者二十五万多倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>在第5章的阶梯上，对两百五十六 MiB 的指针追逐，用两 MiB 的页少花了百分之四十的时间。<bookmark mark='e'/>但大页在只用到一小部分时会浪费内存，而且需要两 MiB 连续的物理页框，繁忙机器上的伙伴分配器未必拿得出来。

3fd23762fa00.en: Research attacks reach from several sides. <bookmark mark='a'/> Direct segments, in 2013: give a big server's heap one base-and-bounds register, beside ordinary paging. <bookmark mark='b'/> Redundant memory mappings: a small TLB of ranges, each covering a large contiguous extent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ingens and HawkEye: policies for when the kernel should promote small pages to huge ones, fairly between processes and without bloating memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> Midgard: let the caches work in an intermediate address space, and translate only on the way to memory. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Mosaic pages, in 2023: restrict each page to a few possible frames, chosen by hashing, so one entry can describe several pages. <bookmark mark='f'/> Notice chapter two's segments returning: a large contiguous range is cheap to translate.
3fd23762fa00.zh: 研究从几个方向进攻覆盖范围问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>直接段，2013年：给大服务器的堆一个基址与界限寄存器，与普通分页并存。<bookmark mark='b'/>冗余内存映射：一个小小的范围 TLB，每项覆盖一大段连续区域。<bookmark mark='c'/>Ingens 和 HawkEye：决定内核何时把小页提升为大页的策略，在进程之间公平，又不让内存膨胀。<bookmark mark='d'/>Midgard：让缓存工作在一个中间地址空间里，只在通往内存的路上才翻译。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有2023年的 Mosaic 页：把每一页限制在通过哈希选出的少数几个页框里，于是一个表项可以描述好几页。<bookmark mark='f'/>请注意第2章的段回来了：一大段连续的范围翻译起来很便宜。

914abe20612a.en: The second frontier is that memory is no longer one thing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Beside the DRAM on the processor's own channels, servers can now attach more memory over CXL, a protocol on the PCI Express link, at two or three times the latency. Beyond that, the disk. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the operating system faces chapter seven's question again, with a new twist: not which page to evict, but which pages deserve the fast tier. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it is nearly blind. The kernel learns about use only from the accessed bits, and to read them fresh it must clear them and flush the TLBs of every core. <bookmark mark='d'/> Meta's TPP, in 2023, demotes cold pages to the slow tier and promotes pages that fault there often; it is now part of Linux. <bookmark mark='e'/> Processors can also sample memory accesses in hardware. How accurately, and how cheaply, the kernel can find hot pages that way is an open question.
914abe20612a.zh: 第二个前沿是，内存不再是单一的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>除了处理器自己通道上的 DRAM，服务器现在还能通过 CXL 接上更多内存，CXL 是 PCI Express 链路上的一种协议，延迟是本地的两到三倍。再往外，是磁盘。<bookmark mark='b'/>于是操作系统再次面对第7章的问题，只是换了个花样：不是换出哪一页，而是哪些页配得上快的那一层。<bookmark mark='c'/>而它几乎是盲的。内核只能从访问位了解使用情况，要读到新鲜的访问位，就得清除它们，并清空每个核心的 TLB。<bookmark mark='d'/>Meta 的 TPP，2023年，把冷页降到慢的一层，把在那里经常缺页的页提升上来；它现在已是 Linux 的一部分。<bookmark mark='e'/>处理器也能在硬件里对内存访问采样。内核能多准确、多便宜地用这种办法找到热页，仍是一个开放问题。

172a058ae5a9.en: The third frontier is the foundations. <bookmark mark='a'/> Page tables are themselves memory. The hardware walker reads them with ordinary loads, while the kernel on another core may be changing them, so translation inherits all the difficulties of Part 10's weak memory models. <bookmark mark='b'/> Only in 2022 did Ben Simner and colleagues publish a precise model of how virtual memory behaves on Arm processors, tested against the hardware and agreed with Arm's architects. <bookmark mark='c'/> Changing a mapping means interrupting every core that might have it cached, a TLB shootdown, which costs microseconds each time and limits how fast many-core systems can remap memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> And verified kernels such as seL4 prove their page-table code correct, against a model of the MMU that must itself be trusted.
172a058ae5a9.zh: 第三个前沿是基础。<bookmark mark='a'/>页表本身就是内存。硬件遍历器用普通的读取来读它们，而另一个核心上的内核可能正在修改它们，所以翻译继承了第10部分弱内存模型的全部困难。<bookmark mark='b'/>直到2022年，本·西姆纳和同事们才发表了一个精确的模型，描述虚拟内存在 Arm 处理器上的行为，经过硬件测试，并得到 Arm 架构师的认可。<bookmark mark='c'/>修改一个映射，意味着要打断每一个可能缓存了它的核心，即 TLB 击落，每次花费几微秒，限制了多核系统重新映射内存的速度。<bookmark mark='d'/>而像 seL4 这样经过验证的内核证明了自己页表代码的正确性，所依据的 MMU 模型本身却必须被信任。

1742198b8d13.en: Six open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> What should replace the four-level radix tree when memories are measured in terabytes? <bookmark mark='b'/> When should the kernel form huge pages, and when break them, trading TLB misses against wasted memory and the cost of compaction? <bookmark mark='c'/> How can it find the hot pages for tiered memory, with bounded overhead and provable accuracy? <bookmark mark='d'/> How much can a learned predictor improve on LRU, while keeping a guarantee when the predictions are wrong? <bookmark mark='e'/> How can TLB shootdowns scale to hundreds of cores? <bookmark mark='f'/> And can a hypervisor with nested paging be verified, on a processor with a weak memory model? <bookmark mark='g'/> This part's research problem takes a small, computable case of the second.
1742198b8d13.zh: 六个开放问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>当内存以太字节计时，什么应该取代四级基数树？<bookmark mark='b'/>内核何时应该组建大页，何时应该拆开，在 TLB 未命中与浪费的内存、紧缩的代价之间权衡？<bookmark mark='c'/>它怎样才能为分层内存找到热页，开销有界而且准确性可证？<bookmark mark='d'/>一个学习得来的预测器能把LRU 改进多少，同时在预测出错时仍保有保证？<bookmark mark='e'/>TLB 击落怎样才能扩展到几百个核心？<bookmark mark='f'/>在弱内存模型的处理器上，带嵌套分页的虚拟机监控器能被验证吗？<bookmark mark='g'/>本部分的研究问题取第二个问题的一个可计算的小情形。

afe31cbb2223.en: What we built in this part. Address translation, from Atlas to the four-level radix tree, and a TLB that makes it nearly free. Page faults, demand paging, and Belady's optimum, his anomaly, and the stack property that rules it out for LRU. Working sets, thrashing, copy-on-write, and the allocators the kernel uses for itself. Virtual machines, from Popek and Goldberg to the nested walk, and containers. And PebbleOS, with an MMU, running every process at the same addresses.
afe31cbb2223.zh: 这一部分我们建造了什么。地址翻译，从 Atlas 到四级基数树，以及让它几乎免费的 TLB。缺页、按需调页，以及贝拉迪的最优解、他的异常，还有排除了 LRU 出现异常的栈性质。工作集、抖动、写时复制，以及内核为自己使用的分配器。虚拟机，从波佩克和戈德堡到嵌套遍历，还有容器。还有带 MMU 的 PebbleOS，让每个进程运行在同样的地址上。

ba5bae34d51b.en: Where this comes back. In Part 33, threads share one address space, which brings races, and the TLB shootdowns we just met. Part 34 adds a disk to PebbleOS, with a page cache and memory-mapped files. Part 35's databases keep their own buffer pool, with their own replacement policy. Part 45 builds the cloud from microVMs and containers. Part 48 meets LRU again, as caches in front of services. And Part 55 attacks memory safety, and the address-space randomisation that defends it.
ba5bae34d51b.zh: 这些内容会在哪里再出现。在第33部分，线程共享同一个地址空间，这带来了竞争，以及我们刚见过的 TLB 击落。第34部分给 PebbleOS 加上磁盘，带页缓存和内存映射文件。第35部分的数据库维护自己的缓冲池和自己的替换策略。第45部分用微虚拟机和容器搭建云。第48部分再次遇到 LRU，作为服务前面的缓存。第55部分攻击内存安全，以及保护它的地址空间随机化。

e4495613a1ed.en: In practice. Look before you tune: the smaps file of a process, vmstat, and perf's count of TLB misses. Databases and Java virtual machines usually want explicit huge pages, and transparent huge pages can cause latency spikes while the kernel compacts memory. When a process vanishes, the out-of-memory killer's reasons are in the kernel log; put limits on control groups rather than relying on swap. A large process's fork copies its page tables, so spawn helpers early, or use posix-spawn. And remember that containers share one kernel: untrusted code belongs in a virtual machine.
e4495613a1ed.zh: 实践中。先观察再调优：进程的 smaps 文件、vmstat，以及 perf 对 TLB 未命中的计数。数据库和 Java 虚拟机通常需要显式的大页，而透明大页可能在内核紧缩内存时造成延迟尖峰。当一个进程消失时，内存耗尽杀手的理由记在内核日志里；给控制组设限，而不要依赖交换。大进程的 fork 会复制它的页表，所以要早点派生辅助进程，或者用 posix_spawn。还要记住，容器共享一个内核：不可信的代码应该放进虚拟机。

d21662ec657c.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: give PebbleOS a copy-on-write fork. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: deciding, with hindsight, which regions deserve huge pages within a budget of wasted memory, the offline version of the question Ingens and HawkEye answer by heuristics.
d21662ec657c.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在本部分的讲义里。可以在任何一题上暂停。第五题是动手题：给 PebbleOS 加上写时复制的 fork。最后一题标着星号，是研究问题：事后回看，决定在浪费内存的预算之内哪些区域值得用大页，这是 Ingens 和 HawkEye 靠启发式回答的那个问题的离线版本。

f988bbf93501.en: Next time, Part 33: Concurrency. Two threads each add one to a counter, and the count goes up by one. Peterson's lock, proved correct, and then broken by the hardware's reordering; locks, semaphores, monitors and deadlock; and the theory of memory models and of which atomic operations can build which. Threads share everything this part worked to keep apart. Part 33, Concurrency.
f988bbf93501.zh: 下一次，第33部分：并发。两个线程各给一个计数器加一，计数却只增加了一。Peterson 锁，被证明正确，然后被硬件的重排打破；锁、信号量、管程和死锁；以及内存模型的理论，和哪些原子操作能构造哪些。线程共享这一部分努力分开的一切。第33部分，并发。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分依据的书籍和论文列在屏幕上和讲义里。感谢观看。
